moduleTitle: Advanced Use Cases - Image-Based Test Automation (IBTA)
learningObjectives: Automate mobile tests using the Image-Based Test Automation method.
Explain when image-based identification is the correct choice and when it is a trap.
Describe what an image-based control actually matches on, and what breaks that match.
Weigh image-based steering against property-based steering for a given control.

elements.text: This independent local guide uses Tosca 2026.1 LTS mobile image-based automation documentation. The original Academy course description, prerequisite licensing and recorded version could not be verified; do not infer a Tosca Cloud prerequisite for every local IBTA test.

elements.title: Create a mobile image-based control
items: Start Mobile Scan, select the application and connect, then choose IBTA Scan.
Use Live mode to navigate, then Scan mode to capture the target area. Switch back to Live mode to interact again.
Choose Button, Textbox or Generic, name the control and configure Accuracy. The documented default is 85%.
Optionally capture additional identifying reference images. Scan Next continues control capture; Finish saves and closes the scan windows.

elements.text: The Mobile Engine does not support Edit images. For resolution variations, configure Tbox_Engines_ImageBased_ImageSearchMethod: MultiScaleTemplate scales images at a performance cost; Feature is an alternative when that method cannot find a match.

bulletPoints: Use the documented capture and additional-identifier workflow.
Resolution adaptation requires validated search configuration; it is not automatic by default.

elements.description: Image matching can help when stable usable control properties are unavailable, including some custom-rendered surfaces. Inspect the actual hierarchy and identifiers first: a canvas, map or chart does not universally imply that no accessible target exists.

A captured target image and optional additional reference images help locate an on-screen control. Accuracy controls how closely the image must match. Successful identification locates a target; separate assertions are still needed to verify business behavior.

elements.text: Properties and image matching use different identification evidence. This local decision guide recommends validating uniqueness, rendering variation and outcome assertions whichever method is chosen.

bulletPoints: Inspect actual properties before choosing image identification.
Additional identifying images can provide reference points; image recognition alone is not a functional assertion.

elements.title: Things that change pixels without changing the control
items: Different resolution or density can change a target’s rendered size. Default search does not resize; test a supported search method for the intended targets.
Theme changes can change the captured reference region.
Font rendering or anti-aliasing can vary across target systems.
Localized text can alter a captured image region.
Visual design changes can reduce image similarity; validate actual accuracy and uniqueness rather than assuming any small change always fails.

elements.text: A changed image match does not by itself classify a product build as passing or failing. Separate expected rendering changes, identification maintenance and actual defects using the requirement and assertion evidence.

elements.description: Higher Accuracy requires a closer match; lowering it allows more differences and may admit unintended regions. Additional reference images and supported resolution search methods can help. Validate both intended matches and competing similar regions; do not blindly lower accuracy until a run passes.

bulletPoints: Rendering variations can affect identification; they do not always break a match or prove a defect.
Validate Accuracy, reference images and supported resolution search methods together.

elements.title: A defensible decision order
items: Inspect properties and verify the scan/context before choosing an identification method.
Assess whether supported stable properties or another well-identified control can reach the target reliably.
If image identification is appropriate, capture a distinguishable target with useful additional reference images.
Validate Accuracy, resolution handling and resulting business assertions on intended device profiles.

elements.text: This is independent maintainability guidance, not a mandatory vendor algorithm or a guarantee that IBTA works immediately. A relative coordinate action also needs validation when layout changes.

bulletPoints: Choose identification based on actual evidence and maintenance risk.
Validate both target recognition and expected behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Treating image-based controls as a general-purpose fallback
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reaching for an image-based control whenever a scan is inconvenient, rather than when the control genuinely exposes no identifying properties.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect actual properties, scan configuration and context before choosing images. Custom-rendered content can still expose accessible targets; validate the specific application.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming an image-based TestCase is portable across devices
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Building image-based steering on one emulator and expecting it to run unchanged on a device with different resolution, density, or theme.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Validate captured images and supported search methods on intended profiles. Rendering differences can affect matching but do not guarantee failure.

examPitfalls.title: Loosening the similarity threshold to fix flakiness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Repeatedly lowering the match threshold until a step stops failing, without checking what else now matches.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Lower Accuracy can admit unintended regions. Validate uniqueness, reference images and rendering differences before loosening it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which situation is the legitimate use case for Image-Based Test Automation?

options.text: A control the scan captured correctly, but whose resource-id is long and awkward to read.
A canvas-rendered chart surface that exposes no accessibility properties or view hierarchy at all.
Any control on a screen where the scan felt slow.
A standard button with a clear accessibility identifier.

practiceQuiz.hint: The question is whether identifying properties exist, not whether they are convenient.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario explicitly establishes no usable properties on the target. Image identification is a reasonable option to validate; convenient property names or scan speed alone do not justify changing strategy.

optionExplanations.A: A long stable ID is still usable property evidence.
optionExplanations.B: This scenario explicitly establishes a target without usable properties.
optionExplanations.C: Slow scanning alone does not establish unsuitable property identification.
optionExplanations.D: A clear usable accessibility ID should be evaluated before replacing it with images.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following can break an image-based control without any defect in the application? (three correct answers)

options.text: Running the TestCase on a device with different screen density
The application switching from light theme to dark theme
Running the same build against a different app language
Adding a bookkeeping step that leaves the target’s rendering and application state unchanged

practiceQuiz.hint: Anything that changes rendered pixels in the reference region is a candidate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Density, theme and localized text can change the reference region and affect identification without a functional defect. The stated bookkeeping step leaves rendering and application state unchanged.

optionExplanations.A: Different density can affect image size and matching.
optionExplanations.B: A theme can alter the captured target appearance.
optionExplanations.C: Localization can change visible target text.
optionExplanations.D: This stated step leaves the target rendering and state unchanged.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An image-based step fails intermittently. A colleague suggests lowering the similarity threshold until it passes consistently. What is the risk?

options.text: The TestCase will execute more slowly.
A looser threshold raises the chance of matching the wrong region, especially where similar visual elements repeat.
The reference image will be deleted automatically.
Image-based controls stop working entirely below a certain threshold.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what else on screen might now clear the bar.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Lowering Accuracy admits less similar regions and can match an unintended target. Validate intended and competing regions rather than assuming every intermittent failure is an accuracy problem.

optionExplanations.A: A universal performance slowdown is not the stated accuracy risk.
optionExplanations.B: Looser accuracy can admit unintended similar regions.
optionExplanations.C: Changing accuracy does not inherently delete the image.
optionExplanations.D: The source does not establish this universal cutoff claim.

quickRecap.value: Capture an image target and optionally additional identifying reference images.
Consider images when usable stable properties are unavailable; inspect the actual target.
Resolution, theme, fonts, language and visual updates can affect matching; validate rather than assuming failure.
Accuracy defaults to 85%; looser settings can admit unintended regions.
Inspect properties/context, then validate the chosen image workflow and business assertions.
Independent local guide using 2026.1 LTS; original Academy prerequisites/version were not verified.
